key_insight: This paper proposes a unified framework that connects neural superposition with sparse, interpretable representations. In simple terms, it shows how latent features in neural networks can be identified, separated, and evaluated in a principled way.
problem_solved: Modern neural networks often mix many features together in hard-to-interpret ways, making it difficult to understand what individual neurons or directions represent. This work addresses the challenge of disentangling these overlapping features and measuring how interpretable they are.
method: Introduces a three-step framework for feature discovery in neural superposition.
Provides a process to identify latent features, disentangle them from mixed representations, and assess their quality.
Frames sparse interpretable codes as part of a broader theory of how information is organized in neural networks.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a clearer path toward interpreting hidden representations in models. It can help improve model transparency, debugging, and analysis of learned features.
visual_elements: A 3-step pipeline diagram: identify → disentangle → assess
A side-by-side comparison of superposed versus sparse interpretable representations
A latent space illustration showing overlapping features being separated
An evaluation chart or scorecard for feature interpretability
paper_title: A unifying framework from neural superposition to sparse interpretable codes
paper_authors: David Klindt, Charles O’Neill, Patrik Reizinger, Harald Maurer, Nina Miolane
